newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil slightly lower in Europe following data.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil slightly lower in Europe following data.

text.p: Palm oil prices were slightly lower at midday in Europe following the easier close in Kuala Lumpur.
European traders had been puzzled by the Malaysian market reaction to the data from cargo surveyors General de Surveillance (SGS) and Caleb Bert.
SGS had put exports during May at 672,805 tonnes while Caleb Bert estimated them at 641,950 tonnes.
Some traders estimated exports at between 630,000 to 650,000 tonnes putting the SGS figure above this.
However, the Malaysian market came down.
"The SGS figure looked supportive at just above the range while Caleb Bert was within it, so we found the reaction in Malaysia a little puzzling," said one trader.
By the close of business in Asia local traders were saying the data was within expectation which led to the lower close.
"They seem to be singing a different song to the one they started with," said another trader.
At midday crude palm oil cif Europe was unchanged after Jun traded at $550.
Among products RBD palm oil was $2.50 down while olein was $2.50 lower to unchanged after Jun traded at $570 a tonne fob Malaysian ports.
Soft oils were 1.50 guilders by across the board supported by higher Chicago soybean futures and a stronger dollar.
Traders said coconut oil appeared to be entering a period of consolidation after the recent volatile trading.
At midday coconut oil sellers were unchanged while palmkernel oil was $2.50 to $7.50 higher.
